mechanism_log: Y1 is driven by all 6 inputs additively (all positive), with X5 and X1 having the strongest effects. Y2 is driven by all 6 inputs additively: X4, X3, X1, X2 decrease it (good), while X5, X6 increase it (bad), creating a conflict with Y1 maximization. Y3 depends ONLY on X1 and X3, with a strong X1*X3 interaction: X1 is monotonically positive, X3 is nonmonotonic (hump-shaped peaking near 0.55), and X1 amplifies the X3 hump (at low X1, Y3 stays low regardless of X3; at high X1, the hump reaches ~0.99). Feasibility requires X1≥~0.4 and X3 in [~0.3, 0.8]. Y4 is driven mainly by X2 and X4 (positive), with moderate X3 effect, weak X1, weak negative X6, and zero X5 effect. The key trade-off is Y1 vs Y2: inputs X5 and X6 push both up, while X1, X3, X4 push Y1 up and Y2 down. Y3 feasibility constrains X1 and X3 to specific ranges.

The system has 6 inputs affecting 4 outputs with a clean separable structure. Y1 is driven by ALL 6 inputs (positive, roughly additive but with superlinear effects at extremes — X5 effect is ~1.08/unit at extreme configs vs 0.75 regression coeff). Y2 is driven additively by all 6: X4 (strongest, negative), X3 (negative), X6 (positive), X5 (positive), X1 (negative), X2 (weak negative). The Y1-vs-Y2 trade-off is primarily mediated by X5 and X6. Y3 depends ONLY on X1 and X3 with zero sensitivity to other inputs; the relationship is a nonmonotonic hump in X3 (peak ~0.55) amplified by X1, but the shape is more complex than a simple parabola — Y3=0.838 at X3=0.80 vs Y3=0.620 at X3=0.775 suggests secondary features. Y4 depends on X2, X4 (primary positive), X3 (moderate positive), X1 (weak positive), X6 (moderate negative), and X5 (zero). The optimal Pareto template is [X1=1, X2=1, X3≈0.80, X4=1, X6=low], varying X5 to trace Y1-vs-Y2 trade-off. X3=0.80 strictly dominates X3=0.55 on ALL objectives.

The system has 6 inputs affecting 4 outputs with a largely additive, separable structure. Y1 is driven positively by ALL 6 inputs, with X5 being the strongest driver (~1.08/unit at extremes, superlinear) followed by X1 (~0.70), X4 (~0.57), X2 (~0.57), X6 (~0.36), and X3 (~0.20). Y2 is driven additively by all 6: X4 (strongest negative, -0.27), X3 (-0.19), X1 (-0.12), X2 (-0.05) decrease it, while X6 (+0.22) and X5 (+0.14) increase it. The Y1-vs-Y2 trade-off is primarily mediated by X5 and X6 since they push both outputs in the same direction. Y3 depends ONLY on X1 and X3 with a strong X1*X3 interaction: X1 is monotonically positive, X3 is nonmonotonic (hump-shaped), and X1 amplifies the hump. The hump peak shifts in X3 as X1 varies — at X1=1.0 peak is near X3=0.55 (Y3=0.987), but the function has complex secondary features (Y3=0.838 at X3=0.80, Y3=0.748 at X3=0.85, sharp drop to 0.136 at X3=1.0). At X1=0.72, X3=0.71 gives Y3=0.927, suggesting the ridge structure shifts. Y4 is driven by X2 and X4 (primary positive, ~0.24 each), X3 (moderate positive, ~0.15), weak X1 (+0.07), moderate negative X6 (-0.10), and zero X5 effect. The optimal Pareto template is [X1=1, X2=1, X3∈[0.80,0.85], X4=1, X5=variable, X6=low], where X5 traces the Y1-vs-Y2 efficient frontier while Y4 remains constant (X5 has zero Y4 effect). X3=0.85 achieves the best Y2 and Y4 extremes while maintaining Y3=0.748 (feasible). Final hypervolume: 1.287.

surprises: X3→Y3 is wildly nonmonotonic: Y3 goes from 0.0 (at X3=0.1) to 0.897 (at X3=0.55) back down to 0.326 (at X3=1.0). The initial correlation of -0.16 completely masked this hump-shaped relationship.

X4→Y1 has a substantial positive effect (OAT range=0.46, gradient=0.50) despite a near-zero correlation (-0.01). The correlation was confounded by X4's simultaneous effects on other variables in the initial random samples.
X2→Y3 and X4→Y3 have exactly zero effect despite moderate correlations (-0.39 and 0.47 respectively) in the initial data. The correlations were spurious.
X3 increases Y1 (OAT range=+0.20) and Y4 (+0.13) and decreases Y2 (-0.17), despite negative correlations with Y1 and Y4 in initial data. Another case of spurious correlations in small samples.
X1→Y2 is a modest negative effect (range=-0.12), contradicting my prediction of 'flat'. X1 slightly helps minimize Y2.
